**1. Is the document accurate? What must be corrected or removed?**

No. Going claim by claim through `docs/release/highlights-v4.md`:

- **"Clinics using v4 see 40% fewer no-shows" (line 5) — unsupported; remove or substantiate.** A case-insensitive search across the entire clinic-portal repository finds this figure only in the highlights document itself. There is no data, analysis, or reference anywhere in the repo backing it, and the repo's single commit is the draft itself. An unsubstantiated quantitative claim should not go to customers.
- **SMS reminders (lines 7–12) — supported, can stand.** `app/notifications/sms.py` implements `SmsSender` with the docstring "SMS sender for appointment reminders (v4)", alongside the existing email sender in `app/notifications/email.py`. The before/after images for this section exist and both show the Reminder Settings page, matching `captures.json` (both captured from `/settings/reminders`). Caveat: the only test in the repo is a placeholder (`tests/test_notifications.py` is just `assert True`), so the feature is untested, but the claim is at least consistent with the code.
- **Scheduling calendar "redesigned end to end (shown with production data)" (lines 14–20) — broken in two ways; fix or cut.** First, the "after" screenshot is not the scheduling calendar at all (see answer 2). Second, "shown with production data" is contradicted by `docs/release/captures.json`, which records `"state": "seed-demo"` for both scheduling captures. I also could not verify the redesign claim itself: the repo contains no scheduling or calendar code whatsoever (grep confirms the terms appear only in docs and the README), and no frontend source despite the README mentioning a React frontend.
- **"Patients can now export their full visit history as a PDF" (lines 22–26) — false; remove.** `app/routers/visits.py` contains only a stub `list_visits` endpoint that returns an empty list, followed by the comment `# TODO: pdf export`. The feature is not implemented. In addition, the section's image `img/after_export.png` does not exist anywhere in the workspace — the email would ship with a broken image — and `captures.json` itself flags it as "expected capture; no corresponding file".
- **"Two-factor authentication is now enabled for every clinic by default" (line 30) — false; remove or rewrite.** `app/security/config.py` sets `TWO_FACTOR_DEFAULT = False` with the comment "Two-factor authentication is opt-in per clinic." The truthful statement is the opposite of what the document says: 2FA is opt-in, not on by default.
- **Footer "Highlights draft assembled with AI assistance." (line 33) — internal note; remove** (detailed in answer 4).

**2. The before/after scheduling comparison.**

The comparison is invalid and must not be sent, for two independent reasons:

- **The "after" image is a screenshot of a different page entirely.** Visually, `img/before_scheduling.png` renders the Scheduling Calendar page, but `img/after_scheduling.png` renders "BILLING / INVOICES". The manifest confirms it: `captures.json` records `before_scheduling.png` as captured from route `/schedule` but `after_scheduling.png` from route `/billing/invoices`. Customers would be shown a billing screen presented as the "redesigned calendar" — the comparison demonstrates nothing about the calendar and is actively misleading.
- **The framing "shown with production data" is false — and would be worse if true.** Both captures are recorded in `captures.json` with `"state": "seed-demo"`, so the parenthetical is factually wrong. And had the screenshots genuinely contained production data, that would mean real patient/clinic information in a marketing email — a serious privacy problem for a clinical product. Either way the parenthetical has to go, and the "after" screenshot must be replaced with an actual capture of the new calendar (or the section cut).

**3. Reconciliation of document images vs. files on disk.**

The document references five images; `docs/release/img/` contains five files — but they are not the same five:

| Image | Referenced in doc | Exists on disk | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `before_reminders.png` | yes (line 11) | yes | Consistent — Reminder Settings, `/settings/reminders`, seed-demo |
| `after_reminders.png` | yes (line 12) | yes | Consistent — same page with the new element |
| `before_scheduling.png` | yes (line 19) | yes | Consistent — Scheduling Calendar, `/schedule` |
| `after_scheduling.png` | yes (line 20) | yes | **Content mismatch** — file exists but shows Billing/Invoices (route `/billing/invoices`), not the calendar |
| `after_export.png` | yes (line 26) | **no** | Missing everywhere in the workspace; `captures.json` explicitly notes "expected capture; no corresponding file" — would be a broken image in the email |
| `unused_capture_07.png` | **no** | yes | Orphan file, absent from both the doc and `captures.json`; it renders as a **"PATIENT LIST"** capture sitting in the customer-facing release assets folder |

So three things don't line up: one referenced image is missing (`after_export.png`), one existing image is referenced but shows the wrong page (`after_scheduling.png`), and one unreferenced patient-list capture is lingering in the release image folder (`unused_capture_07.png`).

**4. Anything else that should not appear in a customer message?**

Yes, three things:

- **The footer "Highlights draft assembled with AI assistance." (line 33).** This is an internal production note — it labels the message a "draft" and discloses the drafting process. Whatever the company's policy on AI-assistance disclosure, a line like this belongs in internal metadata, not in the body of a polished customer announcement.
- **The parenthetical "(shown with production data)" (lines 16–17).** Beyond being false (the captures are seed-demo per `captures.json`), telling clinic customers that marketing screenshots show production data invites the reading that real patient information is being displayed and shared — exactly the wrong signal to send a healthcare audience. Screenshots should use demo data and be labeled as such, or not labeled at all.
- **The unreferenced `img/unused_capture_07.png` ("PATIENT LIST").** It isn't embedded in the document, but it lives in the same `docs/release/img/` folder that would be packaged as the email's assets. A capture named and rendered as a patient list has no place in customer-facing release material and should be deleted from that folder before anything ships (it isn't tracked in `captures.json` either, so nothing accounts for its provenance).

The unsupported "40% fewer no-shows" statistic (answer 1) also belongs in this category: it is a marketing claim with no substantiation anywhere in the repository.
